instructions: Peel the potato and cut it into 1/2 inch cubes. Put the cubes in a small pot, cover them with water and bring it to a boil over high.
Turn the heat down and simmer the potato for 6 to 8 minutes, until a fork goes in easily but the cubes still hold their shape. Drain them and spread them on a plate to cool.

Meanwhile, heat the 2 tbsp oil in a large wide pan over low. Add the 1/4 tsp turmeric, 1/4 tsp chili powder, the pinch of asafoetida and 10 curry leaves. Stir for about 30 seconds, until the leaves crisp up and the spices smell toasty.
Add the 6 cups puffed rice and keep tossing it over low heat for 4 to 5 minutes, until it's evenly yellow and a piece crunches when you bite it.

Take the pan off the heat. Sprinkle over 1 tsp of the chaat masala, the 1/2 tsp cumin, 1/4 tsp black salt, 1/4 tsp salt, 2 tsp sugar and 1/2 tsp amchur, and toss until it's all coated. Leave it in the pan to cool for 5 minutes.
While it cools, finely chop the onion and the 2 tomatoes, and chop 1/4 cup of the cilantro. Finely chop the 2 green chilies and put them in a small bowl for the table. Cut the lemon in half.
Just before you eat, tip the puffed rice into a large bowl. Add the potato, onion, tomatoes, 1/2 cup of the sev and the 1/2 cup peanuts, then crush 8 of the papdi over the top.

Spoon in the 1/4 cup cilantro chutney and 1/4 cup tamarind chutney, sprinkle over the last 1/2 tsp chaat masala and squeeze in the juice of the lemon. Toss gently until everything is coated. Eat it right away. The puffed rice goes soggy within about 10 minutes.
Pile it onto plates and top with the chopped cilantro, the last 1/2 cup sev and the last 4 papdi, crushed.
Serve with the chopped green chilies on the side.
method_notes: Both read versions toss crisp puffed rice with boiled potato, onion, tomato, green chili and cilantro, dress it with green chutney, tamarind chutney and chaat masala at the last minute, and top it with sev and crushed papdi. Hebbar's Kitchen (the lead) first makes a bhel mix by frying the puffed rice in oil with turmeric, chili powder, hing and curry leaves, then seasoning it with chaat masala, cumin, black salt, sugar and amchur, and mixes in fried peanuts, dal, poha and boondi; it finishes with lemon. Swasthi's Recipes only dry roasts the puffed rice if it's gone soft, and makes its own tamarind, green and garlic chutneys. This one follows the lead's spiced puffed rice with store bought roasted peanuts, sev and chutneys in place of the fried extras, and puts the chili on the side.
